newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO STOCKS BOUNCE BACK MILDLY FROM MONDAY'S DROP.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO STOCKS BOUNCE BACK MILDLY FROM MONDAY'S DROP.

text.p: Tokyo stocks recovered modestly on Tuesday from the previous day's nearly four percent plunge in the benchmark index, as stability in the dollar and U.S. stocks prompted investors to bargain-hunt blue-chip exporter issues that had been hit hard on Monday, brokers said.

They agreed that stocks had been oversold on Monday, but the market did not completely recover from the malaise caused by a series of recent figures that showed few signs of a near-term recovery in the economy.
The 225-share Nikkei average finished Tuesday's session up 274.93 points or 1.46 percent at 19,099.11.
Shares of leading high-technology firms, which had tumbled on Monday, perked up.
Leading computer maker Fujitsu Ltd rose 30 yen to 1,610. Its volume of 4.455 million shares was the fifth-heaviest traded issue on the TSE's first section.
NEC Corp, another computer maker, was up 30 yen at 1,560.
Shares in Fuji Television Network Inc extended their gains, rising above the high hit on their first day of trading on Friday, on aggressive buying by brokers on their own accounts, brokers said.
Fuji TV's shares closed 44,000 yen higher at 719,000, after briefly hitting 730,000. The previous high was 700,000 yen.
The second section index finished down 1.63 point at 1,659.23, with 5.36 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 1.26 point at 1,066.29.
